sections.h2: What are the options for selling a house in Sun Prairie?
sections.html:
You can list with an agent, sell it yourself, or take a cash offer on the house as it stands. In Sun Prairie, where the Census median home value is $365,700, the gap between a listing price and a discounted cash price can be large, so run the numbers on each path.

A listing makes sense when the house is move-in ready and you can handle showings. A cash sale is built for situations where time or condition matters more than the top price: an inherited house, a vacant property, deferred repairs, or a move that cannot wait for a buyer's financing.

  • Compare the net after agent fees, repairs, concessions and carrying costs.
  • Confirm who pays for the transfer fee and recording in the written offer.
  • Get any offer in writing with a closing date before you commit.

sections.h2: What does Census data show about Sun Prairie housing?
sections.html:
Sun Prairie grew quickly after 2020. Its 2025 estimate of 39,227 is 9.0 percent above the 2020 base, and the median owner-occupied home is worth $365,700, roughly double the median in Sheboygan or Superior.

About 50.9 percent of adults hold a bachelor's degree or higher, and the poverty rate is 6.2 percent. A city-wide median hides a wide range, so a recent comparable sale on your own street tells you more than any single figure.

The 2020 count of 35,967 compares with 29,364 in 2010, a gain of about 22 percent. Households average 2.35 people, 85.5 percent of residents lived in the same house a year earlier, and 8.9 percent of residents were born outside the United States. Retail sales reached $1.04 billion in 2022, and accommodation and food services sales $119.9 million. Per capita income is $47,609.

sections.h2: What is Sun Prairie like for a home seller?
sections.html:
Sun Prairie is the largest suburb of Madison, in eastern Dane County. The city's land came from the former towns of Bristol, Burke, Sun Prairie and Windsor, and it was incorporated as a city in 1958 after growing from a village incorporated in 1868. Its name comes from a story that a surveying party in 1837 carved the words into a tree when the sun came out after days of rain.

U.S. Highway 151 runs through the city with four access points: Windsor Street, Reiner Road and Grand Avenue, Main Street and Bristol Street. Highway 19 crosses it, and the Badger Interchange of Interstates 39, 90 and 94 is about six miles southwest. The mean commute is 22 minutes, and many residents work in Madison.

The Sun Prairie Area School District runs the public schools. Wikipedia lists nine elementary schools, three middle schools and two high schools for the 2018-19 year, so check the district for current boundaries. Buyers often ask which school their address feeds, so look that up before you list.

sections.h2: Does water or flooding affect Sun Prairie houses?
sections.html:
The city encounters occasional flooding. Sun Prairie lies in the drumlin and marsh area of eastern Dane County, with hydric soils and the Koshkonong Creek nearby, and spring melt adds to the load. A heavy overnight rain on April 11, 2008 outpaced the city's storm drains and flooded residential basements.

If your basement has ever taken on water, say so on the condition report, and keep records of any sump pump, drain tile or waterproofing. The city's building permit list includes drain tile and basement drainage systems, so confirm that work was permitted.

sections.h2: Which Sun Prairie permits and codes should I check?
sections.html:
The city issues single-source building permits through its OpenGov portal, which means one permit covers building, electrical, plumbing and heating on the same project. Your seller file should show a closed permit for any of the following.

  • Roof, siding, fascia and soffit, windows and doors.
  • Furnace, central air, water heater and water softener.
  • Decks, fences, sheds, pools and finished basements.
  • Kitchen and bathroom remodels, plus any electrical, heating or plumbing work.

Flooring, painting, cabinet swaps without plumbing or electrical, and replacing deck boards do not need a permit. Working without one can double the permit fee and add a daily fine. Passing the final inspection is the only way to close a permit, so ask Building Inspection at 608-825-1184 about anything left open.

The property maintenance code applies to owner-occupied homes as well as rentals. Grass and weeds must stay at 8 inches or lower, and sidewalk snow must be cleared within 24 hours after a storm ends. Resolve any open notice before you list.

If you own a rental, the same office handles tenant complaints. When a tenant reports a maintenance problem after the owner has failed to respond, inspectors can visit and send an Official Notice with a deadline to correct it. The city notes that a landlord may not retaliate against a tenant for reporting a violation. The Building Inspection office is at 300 E. Main Street and is open Monday through Friday, 8:00 a.m. to 4:30 p.m.

sections.h2: What do I disclose and pay when I sell in Dane County?
sections.html:
Under Chapter 709, the owner of a one-to-four unit property gives the buyer a completed condition report within 10 days after the contract is accepted. A late report lets the buyer rescind within 2 business days after the 10 days end. Personal representatives, trustees, conservators and court-appointed fiduciaries who never lived in the house are excused.

The state transfer fee is 30 cents per $100 of value, charged to the seller under section 77.22. At the Sun Prairie median of $365,700 the fee is $1,097.10. Of the fees collected, the county keeps 20 percent and the rest goes to the state.

The Dane County Register of Deeds records deeds for a $30 fee per document. The deed must name the grantor and grantee, carry the grantor's notarized original signature, include a legal description and show the parcel number from the tax bill. An electronic transfer return receipt must come with it, and the transfer and recording fees can go on a single check payable to the Register of Deeds.

faqs.q: How much does it cost to record a deed in Dane County?
faqs.a: The recording fee is $30 per document, according to the Dane County Register of Deeds. The state transfer fee is separate, at 30 cents per $100 of value, and both can be paid with one check. An electronic transfer return receipt must accompany the deed.

faqs.q: Do I need a permit history before selling my Sun Prairie home?
faqs.a: Buyers and inspectors ask for it. Sun Prairie issues permits through its OpenGov portal, and Building Inspection at 608-825-1184 can tell you if a permit is still open. Closing open permits before listing keeps the sale on schedule.

faqs.q: What happens if I miss the 10-day condition report deadline?
faqs.a: The buyer may rescind the contract by written notice within 2 business days after the 10-day period ends and is entitled to the return of any deposits. Deliver the completed report early to keep that right from arising.

faqs.q: Can I sell a house in Sun Prairie that has water damage?
faqs.a: Yes. Answer the condition report's questions about water honestly and keep records of any sump pump, drain tile or waterproofing work. A cash buyer purchases as-is and prices the damage in.

faqs.q: Are there rules about parking an RV at my Sun Prairie house?
faqs.a: Yes. The city allows seasonal storage of oversized recreational vehicles from April 1 to November 30 on a paved surface with setbacks and current tags, limited to one oversized vehicle at a time. Neighborhood covenants can be stricter and the city does not enforce them.
